_changes: hash_spec.normalize is now a single ORDERED PIPELINE rather than a set of independent properties. Friday found the third instance of one defect: strip has the same order dependency as lowercase, because a leading space (0x20) sorts below every letter, so an entry with stray whitespace jumps to the front if you sort first. v2 did not specify strip at all, so that entry was simply unhandled.

The general rule, stated once so a fourth instance cannot appear: EVERY step that can alter an entry's bytes must happen BEFORE sort. Listing normalisation steps as unordered properties is what let this recur three times -- case, then whitespace, each found separately. The pipeline formulation makes the ordering unstateable rather than merely stated.
_note: Fingerprint unchanged at 97393204: no current entry has stray whitespace or capitals, so v3 is again a precision change and the stable number is the evidence of that.

normalize_pipeline: 1. strip leading/trailing whitespace from each entry
4. sort ascending by byte order  <- MUST be last; every step above moves entries
5. join with newline as SEPARATOR (no trailing newline)
6. sha256, hexdigest()[:8], as a hex string (not decimal)
hash_spec.invariant: any step that can change an entry's bytes precedes the sort
